title: Uv Editor Improvements | Clo 2025.0 Features Deep Dive
description:
The new update to our UV Editor in CLO 2025.0 allows you to access UV Editor without switching modes, and the side and back UVs can be edited. Check out other new features here: https://www.clo3d.com/en/clo/features

summary: ```markdown # Uv Editor Improvements | Clo 2025.0 Features Deep Dive ## Introduction Hey everyone, it's Phoebe here, and I have some great updates for you regarding our UV editor. So let's jump on in and have some fun while we learn! ## Accessing the UV Editor Here I have a bag, and I want to bring this into another 3D software. I'm going to do that because it's a bag, and sometimes you need some other functionalities that other software provides. To achieve this, I need to use my UV editor to export all the materials properly so that they have the right wrinkling and everything else that I need. ### Location of the UV Editor To access the UV editor, I need to note that it has moved. It is now located in the top toolbar, underneath **Materials > UV**. I'll go to **Materials > UV**, and then I'll see the **UV Editor** right there. After selecting this, my UV editor window will appear. I can resize my UV editor window to make it a bit bigger and easier to see. ## Using the UV Editor All of my patterns and everything I need are in my box right here, which is exactly where I want them. You can, of course, select all of your pattern pieces and use our **Auto UV Packing** feature to automatically pack them inside this area. If needed, you can choose between zero to one or select a tile or anything like that. This is all pretty much set. ## New Features in the UV Editor One of our next really great updates is the ability to select pattern pieces. For example, this fabric is a lining, but the lining is different on the inside. ### Viewing Different Fabrics You can see this if you peek in; you will notice that this is a different fabric. However, right now, it's only showing the top fabric. What I'm going to do is select this pattern piece. If I scroll down to the very bottom of my property editor, I can choose whether I want the back face or side face to be exported as well. - For instance, I will set it to export the back and side for this lining. - I can also do the same for some of my shell fabrics. If I want to have the back of it also showing, I can do that. This means I can select the back and side options to ensure both the back and front are visible for export. ## Exporting Textures and Saving Now, what I can do is take a snapshot. This can be here, or I can also export this out in any file format I prefer. I'm just going to do a quick snapshot. After that, I will hit save and save this into the correct path. Then, I'll have all of my maps saved out for me—pretty easy and great updates! ## Conclusion Thanks so much for watching! If you have any questions, please feel free to use the comment section down below; someone will get back to you. Don't forget to like and subscribe, and definitely check out all of our other videos. There are tons of them on our channel, so keep having fun with Clo! I'll see you next time. Bye! ```
